## Summary

I implemented detection of line breaks in non-triple-quoted f-string replacement fields for Python versions before 3.12.

### Source changes

**`crates/ruff_python_parser/src/error.rs`**
- Added a `LineBreak` variant to the `FStringKind` enum.
- Added its `Display` arm producing the exact message `"Cannot use line breaks in non-triple-quoted f-string replacement fields"` (the framework appends `on Python X.XX (syntax was added in Python 3.12)`). It automatically reuses the existing `Pep701FString(_) => Change::Added(PY312)` version mapping.

**`crates/ruff_python_parser/src/parser/expression.rs`**
- Changed `check_fstring_comments` to return `bool` (whether any comment was found) so the caller can gate the line-break check.
- In the per-replacement-field validation, track whether a backslash was found, then after the comment check, scan the field's source range for `\n`/`\r` with `memchr2`. When the field is **not** triple-quoted, has **no** backslash and **no** comment error, and contains a line break, emit `Pep701FString(FStringKind::LineBreak)` at a single-character range pointing to the opening `{`.
